records.context_summary: Plot two cooling curves with scales, labels, points and best-fit curves
examiner_findings:
ER-2020-061 [commentary; report PDF 475; exact_source_reference] (c) (i)    Very few learners scored full marks in this part. Most learners lost marks for various reasons such as:
               •   Labelling of axes: Many learners swopped the axes although the guidance in the question was
                   clear as to which quantity ought to be labelled on the x-axis and which one on the y-axis as the
                   false origin indicates 0 for the x-axis and 68 for the y-axis. Some learners did not label correctly
                   using the solidus ( / ) or other alternatives to separate the physical quantity and the unit although
                   the conventional guidance of labelling was given in the column headings of Table 3.1.
               •   Scale: Many learners lost marks by using complicated scales which made them struggle to have
                   uniform intervals and as a result, lost marks for the scale. Some learners used small scales which
                   did not cover half of the grid and lost marks. Some learners ignored the guidance which is already
                   given on the grid on Fig. 3.5, for example on the y-axis, instead of continuing the scale from the 68
                   which was already indicated on the false origin for the y-axis, they restarted a scale from 0.
               •   Plotting: Most of the learners who used complicated scales struggled to plot their data according
                   to their scale and lost marks as a result. Some learners struggled to plot points within half a square
                   especially points 80.5, 77.5 and 70.5. Some learners plotted blobs which covered a complete
                   square or more, making it difficult to judge where exactly a particular point was plotted.
               •   Line of best fit: Most of the learners were unable to draw the line of best fit (which is a smooth
                   curve in this case). Many learners lost marks for various reasons such as joining the plotted points
                   dot to dot with a ruler or by free hand, or drawing curves which are waving or feathering.

ER-2021-057 [commentary; report PDF 493; exact_source_reference] (ii)     Poorly answered. Only a handful of candidates scored in the range of 1 to 3 out of 5 marks.

                      candidates left the axes unlabelled altogether while some included wrong units in the label such as°.

ER-2021-058 [commentary; report PDF 493; exact_source_reference] •    Scale: Many candidates lost marks by using complicated scales which made them struggle to have
                      uniform intervals, and as a result, lost marks for the scale. Some candidates used small scales which
                      did not cover at least half of the grid either in the vertical (y-axis), horizontal (x-axis) or both directions,
                      and lost marks. Some candidates ignored the guidance which is already given in the question that
                      they did not need to start their axes at the origin (0, 0).
                 •    Plotting: Most of the candidates who used complicated scales struggled to plot their data according
                      to their scale and lost marks as a result. Some candidates struggled to plot points within half a
                      square (1 mm). Some candidates plotted blobs (very large plots) which covered more than half a
                      small square (1mm) up to a complete square or even more, making it difficult to judge where exactly
                      a particular point was plotted.

records.context_summary: Plan a pendulum investigation with variables, table and conclusion method
creditworthy_points: [AS-15; embedded marking table; report PDF 496] Set up a pendulum.
[AS-15; embedded marking table; report PDF 496] Measure its length.
[AS-15; embedded marking table; report PDF 496] Displace and release it.
[AS-15; embedded marking table; report PDF 496] Time several oscillations and obtain period.
[AS-15; embedded marking table; report PDF 496] Repeat at different lengths.
[AS-15; embedded marking table; report PDF 496] Keep a relevant variable fixed.
[AS-15; embedded marking table; report PDF 496] Specify raw and processed table columns.
[AS-15; embedded marking table; report PDF 496] Explain how the data will test the relationship.
examiner_findings:
ER-2021-068 [commentary; report PDF 495; exact_source_reference] Poorly answered. This question proved that the majority of candidates did not have much exposure to this or a similar
practical activity as they appeared clueless on how to approach the question. The majority of candidates ended up
describing different practical activities such as Hooke’s law.
ER-2021-069 [commentary; report PDF 495; exact_source_reference] The marks were categorised according to marking points (MP) as follow:

ER-2021-070 [commentary; report PDF 495; exact_source_reference] 1   Method: 5 marks
    •   MP1 – this was satisfactorily answered. Many candidates who scored 1 out of 8 marks were able to score
        this mark.
    •   MP2 – this was satisfactorily answered. It was expected that the candidates make reference to measuring
        of the physical quantity (length of string), using the appropriate measuring instrument given in the list of
        apparatus (metre ruler).
    •   MP3 – Poorly answered. The candidates were expected to indicate how to manipulate the setup to carry out
        the experiment by displacing the mass at an angle and release it to oscillate. In most cases, the action was
        missing in this part. Candidates were expected to mention what they would do to initiate the oscillations.
    •   MP4 – Poorly answered. It was expected that candidates make reference to the given measuring instrument
        in the list of apparatus (stopwatch) to measure the physical quantity (time for a number of oscillations).
        Many candidates made reference to measuring only one oscillation. Other candidates made reference
        to measuring time from when the oscillations start up to when the oscillations completely stop. This was
        penalised.
    •   MP5 – Satisfactorily answered. Some candidates were able to indicate that they would adjust the length
        and repeat time measurements as expected. A vague reference to repeats was not sufficient as it is
        not clear whether the candidate was referring to using adjusting the length of the string or repeating the
        measurements of time at the same length. Other candidates missed the point of the aim of the investigation
        altogether and went on to mention adjusting mass instead.

ER-2021-071 [commentary; report PDF 495; exact_source_reference] 2   Control variables: 1 mark
    •   MP6 – Poorly answered. It appears that many candidates did not understand what it means to have control
        variables because they were mostly writing a long list of variables, implying that they will control almost all
        variables in the experiment, which is unexpected. Topic 1.2.1 on page 6 of the 6118 Physics syllabus clearly
        states that learners should be able to “distinguish between dependent, independent and control variables”.
        Candidates were expected to identify at least one variable to keep constant. The mass or angle of swing
        were correct suggestions. Some candidates suggested keeping the length constant and changing mass.

ER-2021-072 [commentary; report PDF 496; exact_source_reference] 3   Table: 1 mark
    •       MP7 – very poorly answered. It was expected that candidates indicate which readings would be displayed
            in their table or tables, which would enable them to investigate whether the length of a string affects the
            period of a pendulum. It was expected that they would have length (of string) and time taken (for a number of
            oscillations) as raw data, as well as period as processed data from the time taken.

ER-2021-073 [commentary; report PDF 496; exact_source_reference] 4   Conclusion
    •       MP8 – very poorly answered. Many candidates could not demonstrate how they would use their data /
            readings to reach a conclusion. Instead, many just quoted the relationship between length and period of
            pendulum from theory, which was penalised.

records.context_summary: Plan a spring extension-load investigation including apparatus, data and conclusion
creditworthy_points: [AS-16; embedded marking table; report PDF 578] Show and label a usable spring setup (two marking elements).
[AS-16; embedded marking table; report PDF 578] Measure the original length.
[AS-16; embedded marking table; report PDF 578] Load and measure the spring.
[AS-16; embedded marking table; report PDF 578] Repeat across several loads.
[AS-16; embedded marking table; report PDF 578] Specify a suitable data table.
[AS-16; embedded marking table; report PDF 578] Specify extension against load or mass on the graph.
[AS-16; embedded marking table; report PDF 578] Explain how the graph establishes the relationship.
examiner_findings:
ER-2022-068 [commentary; report PDF 577; exact_source_reference] This question generally was poorly answered and proved to be the most challenging in the whole question paper. A
large number of candidates scored from 0-4 marks mostly from, MP2, MP4 MP5 and MP7.

ER-2022-069 [commentary; report PDF 577; exact_source_reference] MP1 Candidates could not draw the set up correctly including all apparatus needed; retort stand, spring and mass
hanger. The fact that the spring was not included amongst the listed apparatus, confused learners and they omitted
it in their drawing. Furthermore, a number of candidates could not differentiate between a spring and a string. This
contributed to lose of marks.
MP3 Most candidates could not state clearly the use of a ruler in this experiment.

ER-2022-070 [commentary; report PDF 577; exact_source_reference] MP5. Most learners failed to explain how the experiment should be repeated. They had to add other masses to the
masses already on the mass hanger one by one. Instead learners wrote add 5 x 50g once or repeat the experiment to
make it fair.
MP6. Majority of candidates could not properly label the table. The table should have three columns; mass, length and
extension but most learners could only label two variables.
ER-2022-071 [commentary; report PDF 577; exact_source_reference] MP8. Poorly answered. Candidates could not tell how experimental data could be used to draw a conclusion.

examiner_findings: ER-2023-098 [commentary; report PDF 674; exact_source_reference] Overall, the question was poorly answered as always.

ER-2023-099 [commentary; report PDF 674; exact_source_reference] Mp1 – moderately answered.
Most learners do not know that they were supposed to draw/trace the rectangular transparent block on the paper. Some
learners drew a triangular prism instead of a rectangular block. Most learners lost a mark as they could not mention
where to draw a rectangular block.

ER-2023-100 [commentary; report PDF 674; exact_source_reference] Mp2. Moderately answered. A line was drawn as a dotted line and not drawn perpendicular to a block.

source of light, as a result they ended up mentioning other sources of light e.g. torch.

arrows as a result learners lost a mark.

refraction which was awarded a mark.

ER-2023-102 [commentary; report PDF 674; exact_source_reference] Mp6. Poorly answered. Learners mentioned repeat the experiment but could not mention what needs to change.

records.context_summary: Describe falling acceleration approaching terminal velocity
creditworthy_points: [key; examiner report PDF 653] Single keyed option: D. This records the published key, not an independent scientific verification.
examiner_findings:
ER-2024-004 [commentary; report PDF 653; exact_source_reference] 2.   Very poorly answered

     to gravity. At first, as the object begins to speed up, air resistance increases which reduces the net force on
     the object and decreases its acceleration. When the force of air resistance equals the force of gravity, the

records.context_summary: Plot extension against load with a best-fit line
creditworthy_points: [AS-10; embedded marking table; report PDF 666] Label quantities and units on the required axes.
[AS-10; embedded marking table; report PDF 666] Use suitable scales and adequate grid coverage.
[AS-10; embedded marking table; report PDF 666] Plot all six values accurately (two marks in this scheme).

examiner_findings:
ER-2024-104 [commentary; report PDF 666; exact_source_reference] (c)      There were many well-drawn, accurate graphs with clearly labelled axes. Scales were usually chosen
             sensibly with very few impractical intervals which led to problems with determining more difficult
             positions for plotted points.
             Plotting was mostly careful and many learners indicated the plots with fine crosses. Small dots are
             acceptable but are often obscured when the line is drawn through them, making it more difficult for plotting
             points to be seen clearly. The large or thick crosses and dots (blobs) used by some learners are not
             acceptable as the intended value cannot be determined clearly.
             A sharp pencil should be used for the plots and for the line so that accurate drawing may be achieved and
             errors easily corrected.
             Many learners produced a well-judged straight line as intended and as indicated by their accurate plots.
             However, some joined points together or forced the line through origin when the plots did not justify this.
             The pattern of plots should indicate the trend of the line whether straight as expected or a simple curve.
strong_response_features: Five graph marks cover labelled axes and units, useful scales, accurate points (two marks) and a best-fit line. These are features, not five prose statements.
notes: AO focus is a demand-level judgement, not official part coding or a per-mark allocation; overlapping A/B records must not be summed as separate marks.
Internal evidence only; source question wording must not enter learner-facing resources.

records.context_summary: Plan a volume-cooling investigation with processing and a labelled graph
creditworthy_points: [AS-14; embedded marking table; report PDF 668] Specify the setup and what is varied.
[AS-14; embedded marking table; report PDF 668] Measure the initial temperature.
[AS-14; embedded marking table; report PDF 668] Measure temperature change against timed intervals.
[AS-14; embedded marking table; report PDF 668] Repeat across different water volumes.
[AS-14; embedded marking table; report PDF 668] State a concrete accuracy precaution.
[AS-14; embedded marking table; report PDF 668] Provide a table with quantities and units.
[AS-14; embedded marking table; report PDF 668] Specify a suitable labelled graph.
[AS-14; embedded marking table; report PDF 668] Explain how data or gradients will establish the conclusion.
examiner_findings:
ER-2024-113 [commentary; report PDF 667; exact_source_reference] Many learners did not do well on this question and showed lack of knowledge on experimental techniques. Most
learners had difficulty in interpreting the required practical approach to investigate the given relationship.
The vast majority completed the question.
There were very few detailed, clear, coherent plans for practical work which would investigate the relationship
between volume of hot water and the rate of cooling. Very few learners gained full credit on this question. The mark
scheme also allowed some credit for descriptions which although they may not have satisfied the given brief entirely,
contained aspects of good practice in thermal energy experiment.
The best response showed a logical approach, structured as suggested by the question, with concise sentences
which communicated ideas well. Learners can often miss straight forward points if planning is not approached in a
sequential way.

ER-2024-114 [commentary; report PDF 668; exact_source_reference] The correct required apparatus was often identified, sometimes within the body of the instructions if missing from a
list at the start. A stopwatch was the most common omission. The use of containers that are similar or of the same
material with different volume of hot water was recognized by many.
common_errors: ER-2024-114 [commentary; report PDF 668; exact_source_reference] Triage categories=omission_or_skill_gap,command_word_or_focus_miss; see located finding. Not automatically a misconception.
strong_response_features: The eight marks divide into four method elements, one accuracy precaution, one table, one graph and one conclusion method. This split is specific to this investigation.

              difficult for plotted points to be checked.
           •  Choosing scales such that the plotted points did not span at least half of the given grid.
           •  Forcing the best-fit line to pass through origin, resulting in an inappropriate line
